experiments.scope: Exact recount of the trail search P (proof 2.1) for start lanes 0, 1. Trial 0 runs T1 (the depth-first search of in-kernel cores of at most 10 bits) from bit (lane, z = 0) of each lane of the group, counting every node, and for each core found whose smallest lane is in the group computes C1 (alpha4 compatible with beta3 = T2 leaves), decides P45 > 0 exactly (pruned search over the same alpha4), and, if P45 > 0, computes C2 (beta2 compatible with alpha3 = T3 leaves) and T3's batch layout (proof 2.1: batches and groups). PASS iff the per-lane node counts and the group totals equal GROUP_LOG. The groups 0..3 (lanes 0-1, 2-7, 8-16, 17-24) partition the cores; P45 > 0 is decided by a depth-first search that remembers failed partial states. Other trials return no pair. PASS = (00^135, 01||00^134) satisfies the declared event; FAIL = (00^135, 02||00^134) does not. Both are fixed sentinels, so the host check is vacuous; the evidence is the organizer's execution of the visible code, and the host-counted numbers are successes (PASS) and returned_pairs (PASS + FAIL).
experiments.hypothesis: P's counts that enter the time bound are exact. Predicted: PASS with 692,664 nodes, 1023 cores, sum C1 = 974,737,408, 204 cores with P45 > 0, sum C2 = 608,900,651,514, 2,507,358,321 T3 batches in 616 groups. Over r5-trail-0..3: 8,674,833 nodes, 1741 cores, C1 = 1,639,088,128, 467 kept cores, C2 = 1,379,275,399,350, 5,679,328,446 T3 batches in 1411 groups: the exact counts that P's charge multiplies by counted prices (proof 2.1, 6).

experiments.scope: Counted programs (proof 2.1, 2.4; W operators, load(), st() count 1, test() 2; 256-bit words, bit p = pair or leaf p) and P on sub-problems. First: EQS is a basis of the equations of the 10 round-2 rows. Trials 0, 3, .., 21 (E): seeded basis, x of certificate r5-v6-000038's first message at a seeded slot p; one e_batch and e_control; PASS iff all 24 equation words equal a plain evaluation on a third of the 256 pairs, slot p passes, counts 6,072 and 40. Trials 1, 4, .., 22 (T3): output core, seeded group and Gray position, four t3_batch at seeded thresholds, each with gstep; PASS iff AS of every slot and the pass word equal a plain evaluation, the base is maintained, each batch with its step counts <= 1,583, and over all 513 tau classes the comparison's longest path is 74 and the batch's 1,539, plus 44 for the step. Trials 2, 5, .., 23 (T2): three t2_leaf with steps; PASS iff decisions and digest-plane words equal a plain evaluation, counts <= 166. Trials 24..27 (P as algorithm() runs it, with its F_CAP check): 24: t3_core on core No. 1136 of T1's sorted list from T = 2^30; PASS iff (w1, w2, choice) = (372, 18, 2.4.7.0.4.0) and F = 517 (the native pass-1 line, Appendix A); 25: same core from T = 127; PASS iff no output and F = 0 (native pass 2); 26: trail_search, P's driver, on the sub-problem [core 874, core 1136]; PASS iff output core 874, w1 = 320, w2 = 23, beta2 as in the native pass-1 line (hash B2_874), F = 425; 27: core 1136 with the cap lowered to 100; PASS iff CapReached is raised at F = 101. Other trials: no pair. PASS = (00^135, 01||00^134) satisfies the declared event; FAIL = (00^135, 02||00^134) does not. Both are fixed sentinels, so the host check is vacuous; the evidence is the organizer's execution of the visible code, and the host-counted numbers are successes (PASS) and returned_pairs (PASS + FAIL).
experiments.hypothesis: Prices of proof 6 are the counted longest paths (E 6,112 per 256 pairs on every path, T3 batch <= 1,583, T2 leaf <= 166) and the counted programs compute the plain predicates; the algorithm's Python P takes the native runs' T3 decisions and stops at its cap. Predicted: 28 PASS in 28 returned pairs.

experiments.scope: The B' program bprime() with the R5 constants (no attempt limit per candidate, DMIN 33, D2u weights 1), its budget and its per-candidate cap, both enforced by the counter WK (proof 2.2), executed whole; then the R5 count and the connector with organizer coins. Trial 0: the seed picks one of the R5 runs 21, 24, 42 (q = SHA-256(seed) mod 3; the three runs whose advice came from candidate 0 with B' below 2^23.7 units, so that B' fits the time limit), and B' runs from that run's label ('hashsmash sha3-256-r5 R5 run k') from candidate 0 to its output under the 2^32-unit budget and 2^26-unit CCAP; PASS iff (c, j, DF) and the advice hash equal RUNS[k], the whole-run cost counted by WK equals the R5 log (CHEAP[k], in 1/1355 units) and the facts of proof 3 hold. Trial 1: B' on run 2's label with a 2^22-unit budget and a 2^21-unit candidate cap; PASS iff candidate 0 is stopped by the candidate cap (candidate 1 starts after more than 2^21 and at most 2^21 + 2^13 units), exactly two candidates start, no advice is returned and the cost exceeds the budget by at most one counter update. Trial 2: PASS iff the table RUNS has 48 runs, 46 with an output (each with a status string of length i + 1), and the one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson lower bound of 46 of 48 (exact binomial tail, bisection) is at least 0.40. Trials 3..26: one connector attempt on trial 0's advice with the trial's organizer seed as coins; PASS iff accepted and verify_space holds (Lemmas 1-2 at two random points). Other trials return no pair. PASS = (00^135, 01||00^134) satisfies the declared event; FAIL = (00^135, 02||00^134) does not. Both are fixed sentinels, so the host check is vacuous; the evidence is the organizer's execution of the visible code, and the host-counted numbers are successes (PASS) and returned_pairs (PASS + FAIL).
experiments.hypothesis: Time bound and H1: B' stops each candidate at its cap and the run at its budget; the logged B' runs of R5 are the shipped program's runs; the success count of H1 is the table's. Predicted: PASS on trials 0-2 (trial 0 cost 16,241,153,777, 13,054,253,838 or 13,145,128,283 for k = 21, 24, 42; trial 1: candidate 1 starts 0.68 units above 2^21, cost 2^22 + 188.1 units; trial 2: bound 0.8745); trials 3..26: descriptive acceptance (R5's label-seeded rate was 4,674 of 15,323 attempts, 0.305; proof 4.6 gives the local runs). No bound uses this rate.

experiments.scope: Audit of the R5 study (proof 4.2, 4.3), stratum 0 of 10: the R5 runs 0, 11, 21, 32, 43 (the 45 runs with an output other than run 35, in k order, stratum = position mod 10; run 35's replay needs 113 MB, so its collision is a certificate instead). Trial 0 picks run L[q0], q0 = SHA-256(trial 0 seed) mod n; trial 1 picks a different run, L[(q0 + 1 + SHA-256(trial 1 seed) mod (n - 1)) mod n]. For the picked run k (table RUNS: advice (c, j, DF, hash), first positive space idx, accepting attempt i, coordinate, DF of the space, status string of connector attempts 0..i): B' re-derives the advice from the label 'hashsmash sha3-256-r5 R5 run k' (candidate setup c, attempt j; accepted with the logged DF and advice hash; facts of proof 3); the status string must end with an accepted attempt, contain exactly idx accepted attempts and idx <= 96; the connector attempts i and min(i, 23) others drawn from 0..i-1 with the trial seed (all of 0..i if i < 24) are re-run with the run's coins (label || 'conn' || c + 1, attempt index) and must give the logged status of each; attempt i must be accepted with the logged DF; then the Python E (e_window) runs on the 2^12 aligned coordinates containing the logged coordinate. The trial returns E's first output if every check passes and the output is at the logged coordinate, otherwise no pair. Other trials return no pair. In production the seeds are the organizer's; a holdout nonce changes the picked runs and attempts.
experiments.hypothesis: H1 numerator: the successes in the R5 table are outputs of the specified algorithm (B', connector rule, E) run from their labels, at the logged place among the advice's accepted spaces (index <= 96). Predicted: 2 full 5-round collisions of distinct 135-byte messages.
